ut_reservoir_ridge.blurb: Reservoir Ridge is a quartzite crag beside the Storm Mountain Picnic Area in Big Cottonwood Canyon. Most of the ten climbs are easy bolted lines, with a few trad routes, one winter ice line and a handful of moderate grades: the sport routes sit mostly around 5.6 to 5.7 and the trad lines run from 5.4 to 5.7. The main feature is a broad, laid-back east-facing slab, which picks up shade in the afternoon. The low angle and easy grades make it a friendly spot for newer leaders, and for anyone learning to place gear, since a couple of the climbs let you mix bolts with natural protection.

ut_wall_street_south.blurb: Wall Street South is the downriver end of the big Wall Street cliff band along Potash Road near Moab. It holds ten trad lines on sandstone, with one or two of them going to two pitches. Grades start at 5.9 and run up to 5.13-, with the bulk in the 5.10 range and a smaller group of 5.12 and 5.13 testpieces on top. With nothing easier than 5.9, it suits climbers looking for harder crack and face lines.

ut_fitness_den.blurb: Fitness Den is a short mixed-climbing wall in Provo Canyon, a cave-like feature on the ledge that links the Stairway to Heaven ice cliff with the Bridal Veil side. Ten bolted mixed routes cover M6 to M9, with most at M7 and M8, so it is a place for a hard pump rather than an easy day. The routes are short, protected by bolts the whole way, and reached quickly by traversing the base of the cliff from either direction. It is well suited to practising drytooling and building front-point endurance, and there is still room for more lines in this grade range.

ut_black_and_tan.blurb: Black and Tan is a bouldering sector within Right Fork, one of the Joe's Valley zones near Orangeville in central Utah. Joe's Valley is known for its sandstone, and this sector holds about ten problems. The grades lean toward the easier end, with several in the V0 to V2 range, a few in the middle at V3 to V5, and one harder problem around V7. That mix makes it a reasonable stop for climbers who want a spread of difficulty in one small spot instead of a single hard project.
